statements.quote:
Sample 3 was designed as a constructive replication of Samples 1–2 with three notable exten-
sions: a different AI model (Google Gemini rather than ChatGPT) to test generalizability
across AI systems, a preregistered analysis plan including the median-split homogenization
test, and inclusion of an AI literacy measure and self-report CD items as exploratory mea-
sures.
statements.locator: PDF p. 38, Supplementary Information, Sample 3 Methods, Design Features

statements.quote:
The full preregistration is available at https://aspredicted.org/wv4yv5.pdf. Preregistered
hypotheses included: (1) CD predicts product creativity, (2) CD predicts output diversity
via the median-split cosine similarity test, and (3) CD shows discriminant validity beyond
interaction quantity. Power analysis targeted N = 165 to yield approximately 140 in the
analytic sample, providing at least 89% power for all three hypotheses based on Sample 2
estimates (r = .31 for CD–creativity, d = .77 for homogenization).
statements.locator: PDF p. 38, Supplementary Information, Sample 3 Methods, Preregistered Hypotheses and Power

statements.quote:
Four exploratory measures were preregistered for Sample 3 and are reported here: self-report
Creative Direction, AI literacy, copy-paste behavior, and GPTZero AI-detection scoring.
statements.locator: PDF p. 38, Supplementary Information, Sample 3 Methods, Exploratory Measures

statements.quote:
We analyzed the open-domain WildChat-1M corpus (Zhao et al., 2024), which contains
1,000,000 real-world conversations with ChatGPT collected in April 2024. The corpus in-
cludes conversations with multiple GPT model versions: GPT-3.5-turbo (variants 0301,
0613, and 0125; 73% of the final sample) and GPT-4 (variants 0314, 1106-preview, and
0125-preview; 27%). It includes metadata (language, country, toxicity flags) and full chat
transcripts. Creative-intent labels were provided by a supplementary dataset (heyyjudes/
wildchat-creative-only-labeled).
statements.locator: PDF p. 40, Supplementary Information, Sample 4 Methods, Source Dataset

statements.quote:
For product scoring, WildChat did not contain separately submitted final responses,
so a product turn first had to be inferred from the conversation itself. In Stage 2, three
LLM judges independently selected which assistant turn best represented the user’s final
creative product; the bundled data retain these selections as anthropic_product_turn,
google_product_turn, and mistral_product_turn. The majority-vote product turn was
extracted and scored by the three product models using WildChat task-type prompts (story,
script, fan fiction, worldbuilding, poem, song, or letter). The 10–50 scale and core creativity
criteria were otherwise the same as Samples 1 and 2.
statements.locator: PDF p. 42, Supplementary Information, Process and Product Scoring in WildChat

statements.quote:
Unique users were identified via hashed IP addresses provided in the WildChat-1M metadata.
A lookup table mapping conversation hashes to hashed IPs was used for participant-level
aggregation. This is an imperfect proxy for individual identity (multiple users may share an
IP; one user may use multiple IPs), but represents the best available identifier in the dataset.
statements.locator: PDF p. 42, Supplementary Information, User-Level Aggregation

rows_checked and columns_checked refer specifically to data/sample1/creativity_scored_20260225_063157.csv. Its 936 rows represent 234 people, each observed in both chat and solo conditions for both dpt (design problem) and title tasks. Each of the four task-by-condition cells has 234 distinct user_id values, nonmissing user_response and all three product scores. There are no duplicate user_id/task/condition keys and there are 234 matched chat/solo pairs per task. Thus has_arm_assignment=true means observed condition labels are available; it does not establish randomized order or allocation. The CSV does not contain an allocation/order variable.

S1 process file contains 413 engaged chat observations (223 dpt, 190 title) from the same 234 people; all join to product scores on user_id/task/condition. It includes response text, chat transcripts and measured CD. Do not restrict the full chat-versus-solo product comparison to these 413 CD-scored rows without an explicit analytic reason.

S2 process file has 656 task rows from 205 people, 655 nonmissing final responses; joining to the product-score file on participant_id/task_num yields 655 scored observations from 205 people. The product file itself has 864 rows from 227 people and no duplicate participant_id/task_num keys, so its raw count is not the manuscript analytic count. Human ratings contain 6,830 rater-item rows from 205 participants; condition=process/product distinguishes what raters scored, not treatment assignment. The 215-row covariate file is also not itself the 195-person complete-data analytic subset. Apply the documented joins, no_interaction filter and missingness rules.

S3 sample3_analysis.csv contains 422 outputs from 157 participants with response, chat_transcript, task_number/task_label, mean_creative_direction, per-model creativity scores and avg_creativity. within_group_similarity.csv has 422 rows and includes cd_group (Low=249 rows; High=173 rows) and within_group_sim; these are measured-CD groups, not randomized arms. S2 and S3 share one AI-access condition within each sample.

S4 process file contains 6,290 conversation hashes and 2,053 distinct non-null hashed_ip identifiers; the product file contains 5,772 conversation rows and joins to the process file on conversation_hash. The inspected files include scores, model/task metadata and product_turn but no full chat transcripts or selected product text. The three separate anthropic_product_turn/google_product_turn/mistral_product_turn fields claimed in PDF p. 42 are not columns in these inspected S4 CSVs. There is a single product_turn column in each. hashed_ip is only a proxy for people.

data/sample4/wildchat_hashed_ip_lookup.csv is 82,122,950 bytes according to the tree API and was not downloaded because it exceeds 20 MB. The reproduction loader replaces process-file hashed_ip values with this lookup; exact equivalence of those mappings was not checked. Existing non-null hashed_ip values permit aggregation of the inspected data, but exact replication of the paper's S4 user sample has not been verified. Source WildChat corpus deposits are inventoried separately; their large text shards were not downloaded.

notes:
Checked 2026-10-09. Read the entire 89,460-character markdown conversion, including all appendices/Supplementary Information (PDF pp. 1-48), in successive chunks. Quotes are exact PyMuPDF text substrings, retaining PDF line wraps and printed hyphenation. The broken-looking GitHub URL in the quote is confirmed by the PDF hyperlink annotation and the live repository, not guessed. No other data/code availability statement or request-only access condition was found in the paper.

The supplied forms/c205.json has no final object and therefore no final.open_items list; open_questions is empty. what_we_could_compute is null solely because an item-by-item mapping to that absent list cannot be made. The brief's requested calculations are nevertheless supported as described below.

Confirmed feasible for S1 from inspected participant-linked output rows: per-person mean creativity within chat and solo conditions (and separately by task), arm/condition means, between-person SDs, SEs and analyzed participant counts; matched-pair counts, within-person differences and their SD/SE; and new within-condition/task diversity measures from the final response texts. Creativity can be formed from openai_score, qwen_score and xai_score using the authors' documented averaging. S1 observed-CD group statistics are also feasible after joining the 413 engaged chat rows to product data. Counts and eligibility must follow the chosen outcome's inclusion rules.

Confirmed feasible for S2 and S3: person-level creativity means/SDs/SEs and analyzed counts after applying documented joins and exclusions; observed high/low-CD group counts, creativity summaries and diversity measures from final response text. S3 additionally includes participant-linked within_group_sim and cd_group for the reported diversity analysis. Human ratings for S2 are public and can be aggregated over raters/items/persons after the no_interaction filter. These are measured-CD comparisons within common AI access, not assigned-arm effects.

S4 public scored conversations and hashed user identifiers support descriptive outcome aggregation, subject to the lookup-mapping limitation noted in the GitHub entry. Exact participant identity is not established by hashed IP. S4 diversity is not directly computable from the inspected GitHub CSVs because they lack the full products/transcripts; reconstruction would require joining to the upstream corpus, whose large files were not read under the 20 MB limit.

Data availability does not resolve randomization eligibility. The form and PDF leave S1 allocation/order randomization unstated despite counterbalancing. S2 and S3 do not randomize AI access or CD; the S3 preregistration randomizes task order only. S4 is observational. has_arm_assignment=true in the GitHub entry applies to explicit S1 chat/solo condition labels.

Six deposits/resources are inventoried: the usable GitHub data repository, the AsPredicted protocol, an OSF manuscript project, and three upstream WildChat resources. Only the GitHub deposit establishes public participant-linked outcomes and conditions. No unpublished matching data deposit was identified in the DataCite, Zenodo or Harvard Dataverse results inspected; the exact-title OSF result contains only the paper. Broad surname queries were refined rather than treated as exhaustive. All remote access used Python urllib with User-Agent atlas-screening/0.1 and no personal identifier; no login, account creation or access request was made. Data files were read only in memory.
